notes: MongoDB 7.0+ OS lists come from the live pages https://www.mongodb.com/docs/community-platform-support/ and /enterprise-platform-support/ (columns 9.x, 8.x, 7.x). The 8.x column is shared by 8.0, 8.2 and 8.3; the docs have no per-minor table. The 8.0 and 7.0 lists match the versioned install pages (/docs/v8.0/tutorial/install-mongodb-on-*/ and /docs/v7.0/...).

/docs/manual/ is 9.0 ('Version 9.0 (current)'). /docs/v8.2/, /docs/v6.0/, /docs/v5.0/, /docs/v4.4/ and /docs/v9.0/ production-notes URLs redirect to /docs/manual/. Production notes for manual, v8.3, v8.0 and v7.0 contain no OS table; they link to the platform-support pages.

MongoDB 3.6-6.0 lists come from the mongodb/docs GitHub branches: v3.6/v4.0/v4.2 source/includes/fact-platform-{x86_64,arm64}.rst; v5.0 and v6.0 source/includes/platform-support.rst (the v5.0 file carries the 4.4 column).

MongoDB Rocky/Alma/Oracle Linux ids are included only where the row label names them. Oracle Linux appears only in x86_64 rows, and only with the Red Hat Compatible Kernel: 'MongoDB only supports Oracle Linux running the Red Hat Compatible Kernel (RHCK). MongoDB does not support the Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel (UEK).' Rocky/Alma footnote: 'MongoDB on-premises products released for RHEL version 8.0+ are compatible with and supported on Rocky Linux version 8.0+ and AlmaLinux version 8.0+, contingent upon those distributions meeting their obligation to deliver full RHEL compatibility.'

Notable MongoDB drops: RHEL/Oracle Linux 7, Amazon Linux 2, SLES 12 and Debian 11 are listed for 7.x but not 8.x. Ubuntu 18.04 and Debian 10 stop after 6.0. Ubuntu 20.04 stops after 8.x (not in 9.x). Amazon Linux 2023 first appears for 7.0 (not in the 6.0 column). RHEL 9 starts at 6.0.4, Ubuntu 22.04 at 6.0.4, Ubuntu 24.04 at 8.0, Debian 13 and SLES 16 at 9.0, Ubuntu 26.04 at 9.0.4.

MongoDB minimum CPU: 5.0+ needs AVX on x86_64 and ARMv8.2-A on arm64 (production notes): 'Starting in MongoDB 5.0, mongod, mongos, and the legacy mongo shell no longer support x86_64 platforms which do not meet this minimum microarchitecture requirement.'

MongoDB 9.0 Linux kernel warning (production notes): 'running MongoDB with a Linux kernel version from 6.19 through 7.0.13 can cause MongoDB to crash ... MongoDB detects these kernel versions and stops during startup.'
MongoDB ids 'rhel6', 'amzn1', 'debian8', 'ubuntu1404' and 'sles11' have no normalized id in this file; they are listed under other_listed_x86_64 or other_listed.
Extra ids beyond the requested list (rhel10 clones and new releases): rocky10, alma10, ol10, ubuntu2604, sles16. They are added because the official tables list them.

PSMDB: the system-requirements pages (4.4-8.3) give CPU requirements only, no OS table. The OS table lives at https://www.percona.com/release-lifecycle-percona-software-for-mongodb/ (linked from the lifecycle page https://www.percona.com/services/policies/percona-software-support-lifecycle), and today it only has 'PSMDB 7.x' and 'PSMDB 8.x' columns. PSMDB 3.6-6.0 lists come from Wayback Machine snapshots of the official lifecycle page (web.archive.org URLs in sources).

PSMDB lifecycle states (official definitions): Active = 'Actively releasing new builds'; Extended Support = 'New builds only for critical bug fixes or security issues'; EOL = 'No new builds, existing downloads available'; NA = 'Builds were never available on this platform'. The x86_64 lists here keep OSes that were 'Active' for that series in at least one official table.

PSMDB Rocky/Oracle Linux: 'We support and test Percona Software for MongoDB on Rocky Linux and Oracle Linux, following the same Application Binary Interface (ABI) compatibility policy as RHEL.' AlmaLinux has a row only for version 10. Older snapshots have RHEL rows only, so clones are not listed for PSMDB 3.6-6.0.

PSMDB Amazon Linux 2023: 'Amazon Linux 2023 is available starting with the following product versions: PSMDB 6.0.20-17, PSMDB 7.0.16-10, PSMDB 8.0.4-2'. Per-version AL2023 compatibility tables are on /install/amazon-linux.html; each PSMDB build only works on specific AL2023 releases.

PSMDB 8.2 and 9.0 do not exist: the lifecycle table lists PSMDB 3.2-8.0 and 8.3, and docs.percona.com has no 8.2 or 9.0 system-requirements page (404). MongoDB 8.2 docs have been removed (redirect to manual).
PSMDB 6.0 RHEL 9 cell reads 'Active1' in the Apr 2024 snapshot; the footnote text is not present in that snapshot.
